title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornography featuring real people's faces was deployed at scale on a website attracting 13 million monthly visitors. The system created a harm that existing legal and technical safeguards did not prevent. Dutch celebrities, politicians, and members of the royal family discovered their likenesses in explicit content they did not consent to create. This is a straightforward failure of a generative system deployed without meaningful restriction on its use.

The harm occurred because nobody with authority to stop it intervened before the videos spread. Creators remained anonymous and profited from views. A technical check at the platform level, or rapid takedown procedures once victims reported content, could have limited damage. Whether either existed is not established from the reporting.

The incident shows that legal prohibitions on nonconsensual deepfake pornography do not automatically stop production where anonymity is possible and financial incentive exists. Victims had recourse only after harm occurred, including police reports and lawsuits. One prior case resulted in a conditional sentence, but enforcement appears insufficient to deter future creation.

summary:
Multiple female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces on a website that attracts 13 million monthly visitors. The platform contains numerous fake videos depicting Dutch artists, TV presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government officials, and members of the royal family. Acting Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos appalling and urged victims to file reports. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to NOS that they have filed complaints or are pursuing legal options.

These deepfake pornographic videos work by digitally placing a celebrity's head onto footage of adult performers. Creators of the content remain anonymous to avoid prosecution and earn money based on video views. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake pornography featuring celebrities will emerge. Deepfakes fall under revenge porn laws and are criminal offenses. Victims can file police reports, pursue class action lawsuits, file complaints with data protection authorities, or contact hosting companies. A previous case involved TV presenter Welmoed Sijtsma, whose attacker received a conditional 180-hour community sentence in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
